target_customer: Indian engineering students and graduates, plus colleges and employers buying training and hiring services
problem: Indian engineering graduates often lack industry skills, and college curricula do not teach tools like CAE and CFD used by employers.
business_model: Paid online courses with placement support, university partnership programs, corporate training and hiring services

founders.name: Surya Paneerselvam
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page. A search summary attributed prior jobs at Cummins and a University of Wisconsin-Madison master's to the founders, but that came from a snippet of an unopened source, so it is not recorded.

founders.name: Sarang
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page as Sarang; surname not confirmed from an opened source.

competitors.name: upGrad
competitors.what: Online higher education and upskilling programs in India
competitors.traction_then: gross revenue about INR 57 Cr in March 2018
competitors.funding_then: venture backed, amount conflicts by source

competitors.name: Great Learning
competitors.what: Gurugram edtech upskilling in data and tech with corporate partners
competitors.traction_then: about Rs 150 Cr revenue, bootstrapped, 60,000 learners impacted

technical_complexity.rationale: Video courses, projects and a learning platform; the hard part was curriculum quality and instructor supply rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Content is copyable and many Indian edtech players competed; partnerships with IIT programs and placement networks add some stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquirer of Skill-Lync found; instead Skill-Lync acquired Crio in November 2022 and cut staff in 2023.

market_need_then: Large pool of Indian engineering graduates with skill gaps and strong edtech funding interest; the founders began by teaching on Facebook and YouTube (YourStory 2022, from search summary).

identity.voice_and_tone: Outcome driven: 'Become the engineer industry hires'

branding.brand_signature: Tagline 'Engineering, the way industry does it'
branding.community_and_virality: Started as a Facebook group and YouTube channel per a search summary of YourStory; unverified from an opened page.

brand_strength.rationale: Hyphenated name with an odd spelling and no sourced brand press, though the community origin helped early reach.

outcome_analysis: Skill-Lync grew to a listed team of 3,000 and raised a $17.5M Series A in August 2021 led by Iron Pillar. It then absorbed Crio in November 2022 and, as the edtech funding environment collapsed, laid off hundreds of staff in 2023 across several rounds. It is still listed as active, so it stalled in growth rather than failed.
notes: Series A is reported by many outlets (YourStory, Business Standard, Entrackr, Entrepreneur India); one report puts Iron Pillar's share at $15M. A total of about $20M implies a seed near $2.5M, which only an aggregator mentions, so it is not recorded as a round. The Crio acquisition and 2023 layoffs are from search summaries and the YC page, not opened articles. Competitor sources are dated 2019-05 and 2019-09, a few months after the batch start.
